text:
Never drafted, Frederick Gaudreau made it to the NHL as a free agent, and at 33 he is having the scoring run of his career in Seattle. He has 8 goals in 19 games after 7 in all of last season.

The finishing is the whole story, and it is the part that rarely lasts. Those 8 goals came on 3.8 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he is shooting 38% on just 21 shots, against 10% last season. Our range for his shooting runs from about 12% to 17%. The goals that are already in count, but the pace does not.

What worries us more is the territory. The Kraken take only 34.8% of the 5v5 shot attempts with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 4% of forwards for creating offense last season, partly because he plays with weaker teammates. He kills penalties and shoots rarely. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with a habit worth watching: 20% of his setups come from behind the net, like the one Alison Lukan noted on a recent hat trick. Our range for his season is 33 to 51 points.
